title: Where the code step lives, and what stays out
synthesis: You want a second factor that needs **no app install**, and you would rather ship a narrow version in two weeks than a complete one in six.
That makes recovery and scope the open questions: both decide how much of the sign-in flow has to change.

questions.title: Where does the person enter the emailed code?
questions.why: This decides whether the existing sign-in form changes or stays as it is. A second screen is easier to add but is one more page load on every sign-in.

options.label: On the sign-in form
options.description: The code field appears under the password once the password is accepted.
gives: One screen from start to finish
costs: The form has to handle a half-signed-in state

recommendation.reason: `LoginForm` has no notion of a partly signed-in session, so the second screen is the smaller change.

questions.title: How often should a returning person be asked for a code?
questions.why: Asking every time is the safest and the most annoying. Remembering a device trades a little safety for far fewer codes.

recommendation.reason: Re-asking every 30 days is the usual middle ground.

figures.title: How many codes would a returning user enter?
figures.source: Illustrative model · five weekday sign-ins per week on one device, starting on Monday. Trust persists for the selected duration.
figures.caption: In this scenario, remembering the device for a month avoids 19 prompts. It also leaves a longer interval before the next code check.

figures.title: Where the user chooses to trust a device
figures.alt: Verification form with a six-digit code field and an unchecked Remember this device for 30 days checkbox above Verify.
figures.source: Chromium capture of a local verification-screen prototype. Proposed design.

callouts.text: Trust requires an explicit choice. Leaving this unchecked keeps a shared device on the every-sign-in policy.

questions.title: What is in this pass, and what is not?
questions.why: Everything you move out of the first pass becomes a stated non-goal in the plan, with the reason you give.

rows.label: Backup codes
rows.description: Printed codes for when email is unreachable.

rows.label: Admins can require 2FA for a team

recommendation.reason: Remembered devices follows from your answer on friction; SMS brings a vendor and a cost that nothing here asks for.

questions.title: Sessions already record when a second factor passed
questions.why: If this is right, the data model needs no migration and the plan can skip it.
questions.statement: The `sessions` table has a nullable `mfa_verified_at` column that nothing writes to yet, so a verified code can be recorded there.
